name: HGH 191AA

b.x: Sleep gets deeper within days. That's the first thing most users notice after starting HGH 191AA, the full-length 191-amino-acid recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin, CAS 12629-01-5). The compound is bioidentical to endogenous GH produced by the anterior pituitary. Unlike secretagogues such as ipamorelin or CJC-1295 that signal the pituitary to release stored GH, exogenous somatropin bypasses the signaling chain entirely. Each injection delivers a known quantity of growth hormone directly into circulation. Subcutaneous bioavailability runs about 70 to 80 percent on US labels, and serum levels peak about 4 to 6 hours after the injection. The terminal half-life after a subcutaneous dose is 2 to 4 hours [1]. The FDA has approved multiple somatropin brands for adult growth hormone deficiency (GHD). Norditropin's current label (July 2025) starts adults at about 0.2 mg a day, within a 0.15 to 0.3 mg range. The dose then rises by 0.1 to 0.2 mg every 1 to 2 months, guided by response and IGF-1. Community protocols run considerably higher. Across r/PEDs, bodybuilding forums, and anti-aging communities, 2 to 4 IU per day (667 to 1333 mcg) is the standard body-recomposition dose, with advanced users pushing 4 to 6 IU. Real-world results track a predictable pattern: sleep improvement in weeks 1 to 2, recovery gains by week 3, visible fat loss by weeks 6 to 10, and peak body composition changes at weeks 9 to 16. Insulin resistance is the main metabolic risk above 2 IU per day. Fasting glucose can rise 10 to 20 mg/dL, making regular blood work non-optional at any dose.

Somatropin binds the growth hormone receptor (GHR), a type I cytokine receptor found on hepatocytes, adipocytes, myocytes, and chondrocytes. Receptor dimerization activates the JAK2-STAT5 signaling cascade. This triggers transcription of IGF-1 in the liver, which mediates most of the downstream anabolic and metabolic effects. The lipolytic pathway is direct and GH-receptor-dependent. GH activates hormone-sensitive lipase in adipose tissue, breaking down stored triglycerides into free fatty acids. This is why morning fasted dosing is popular in community protocols; it amplifies the fat-mobilizing window before carbohydrate intake blunts the effect. GH also stimulates chondrocyte proliferation and collagen synthesis in connective tissue. Bone mineral density moves more slowly. In the Genotropin label's adult trials, it dipped after 6 months of treatment and was back at baseline by 12 months. Protein synthesis in skeletal muscle increases through both direct GHR activation and IGF-1-mediated mTOR pathway signaling. The negative feedback loop matters. Exogenous GH suppresses hypothalamic GHRH secretion and upregulates somatostatin release. This blunts endogenous pulsatile GH output during use; periodic off-cycles allow the hypothalamic-pituitary axis to recover its natural rhythm.
HGH 191AA benefits center on direct, dose-dependent growth hormone elevation with predictable outcomes.
Fat loss becomes visible around the midsection by weeks 6 to 10. In two 6-month Norditropin label trials in adults with GHD, total body fat fell about 4 to 5 percentage points more than on placebo.
Sleep depth improves within the first week. Community reports across thousands of user logs on r/PEDs consistently describe faster onset and longer deep-sleep phases, especially with pre-bed dosing.
Skin elasticity and hydration measurably improve by weeks 8 to 12, a finding corroborated in both GHD replacement studies and anti-aging community use.
Workout recovery shortens noticeably by weeks 3 to 4. Users report returning to training faster and with less soreness.

Connective tissue strengthens over longer cycles, as IGF-1-mediated collagen synthesis supports joint repair. Bone density moves more slowly. In the Genotropin label's adult trials, it dipped at 6 months and was back at baseline by 12.
Lean mass preservation during caloric deficit is one of the most valued effects in recomposition protocols; GH shifts fuel utilization toward fatty acid oxidation, sparing muscle protein.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 10 key studies · FDA-approved
Exogenous recombinant somatropin is the gold-standard, FDA-approved treatment for adult GHD with strong Phase 3 evidence.
Dosing studied: 0.15–0.3 mg/day start (0.45–0.9 IU/day), raised 0.1–0.2 mg every 1–2 months, for adult GHD (Norditropin label); up to 2 mg/day (6 IU/day) in off-label performance contexts
Off-label body-composition and anti-aging use shows real but modest benefits in healthy adults. Performance-enhancement evidence is weak despite clear anabolic mechanism.

Limitations

High-quality RCTs cover diagnosed GHD populations almost exclusively. Healthy-adult body-composition trials are small and short-duration. Long-term safety of supraphysiological dosing (community 2–6 IU/day) is not formally studied. Cancer risk via sustained IGF-1 elevation is a real concern with chronic high-dose use.
Community Experience
Universally regarded as the most reliable and direct GH elevation method: preferred over secretagogues for predictability and potency.
Community dosing: 1–4 IU/day (333–1333 mcg/day) for most use cases; 4–8 IU/day reported in advanced bodybuilding
Heavy use across anti-aging, body-recomposition, and competitive bodybuilding communities.

Science firmly supports GHD-replacement dosing, which starts at 0.45–0.9 IU/day on the Norditropin label (0.3–1.5 IU/day by age in AACE 2019 guidelines). Community protocols routinely run 2–6 IU/day for body-composition purposes: about 3–10× the label's typical 0.6 IU starting dose. The anabolic mechanism is fully understood, but no high-quality RCTs exist in healthy adults at community-level doses. Real benefits are plausible and user-reported, but risk profile scales with dose.
Community Somatropin: community dosing consensus

The IU-to-mcg conversion trips up most beginners: 1 IU equals roughly 333 mcg. A 10 IU vial holds about 3.3 mg of somatropin. A 15 IU vial holds roughly 5 mg. Reconstitution math for the standard 10 IU vial: add 1 mL bacteriostatic water. That gives you 10 IU per mL. On a U-100 insulin syringe, 10 units equals 1 IU (333 mcg). For the beginner dose of 200 mcg (0.6 IU), draw 6 units. Moderate dose of 500 mcg (1.5 IU) is 15 units. Aggressive dose of 1000 mcg (3 IU) is 30 units. Swirl the vial gently after adding water. Never shake or vortex somatropin; the protein is fragile and shaking creates dimers that increase side effects. Store reconstituted vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and use within 14 to 28 days, depending on the product label. Lyophilized (powder) vials also belong in the fridge. Never freeze reconstituted HGH. Morning fasted injection maximizes fat mobilization. Pre-bed injection amplifies the natural nocturnal GH pulse and tends to improve sleep quality. Split dosing (AM plus PM) is common at 3 IU per day or above.
HGH 191AA Cycle

Exogenous HGH suppresses endogenous pituitary GH secretion via negative feedback on GHRH and via somatostatin upregulation. Long-term continuous use blunts natural pulsatile GH secretion. Periodic off-cycles allow the hypothalamic-pituitary axis to recover, IGF-1 to normalize (reducing sustained cancer risk), and provide a monitoring window to detect glucose or metabolic changes. Antibody formation against exogenous GH is rare with high-purity preparations but can occur with gray-market products: an off-cycle allows detection if efficacy diminishes.
Diminishing fat-loss or body-composition response despite maintained dose (possible tachyphylaxis or antibody formation)
IGF-1 not rising proportionally to dose increase (possible antibody interference: more likely with gray-market product)
Persistent insulin resistance or fasting glucose elevation despite dose optimization
Carpal tunnel or water retention not resolving with dose reduction
Gather supplies: one vial of lyophilized HGH 191AA, bacteriostatic water, a U-100 insulin syringe (29 or 31 gauge, 0.5 inch needle), and alcohol swabs.
Clean the top of both the HGH vial and the bacteriostatic water vial with alcohol swabs. Let them air dry.
Draw 1 mL (100 units on the syringe) of bacteriostatic water. For a 10 IU vial, this gives 10 IU per mL. For a 15 IU vial, this gives 15 IU per mL.
Inject the water slowly down the inside wall of the HGH vial. Do not spray it directly onto the powder. Let gravity pull the water down; tilt the vial if needed.
Swirl gently until the powder dissolves completely The solution should be clear. If it stays cloudy after five minutes, the product may be degraded. Do not use a cloudy solution.
Draw your dose For a 10 IU vial reconstituted with 1 mL: beginner 200 mcg (0.6 IU) equals 6 units; moderate 500 mcg (1.5 IU) equals 15 units; aggressive 1000 mcg (3 IU) equals 30 units.
Pinch a fold of skin on the abdomen (avoiding a 2-inch radius around the navel), thigh, or glute. Insert the needle at a 45 to 90 degree angle. Inject slowly. Rotate sites each injection.
Timing depends on your goal Morning fasted for fat loss prioritization. Pre-bed for sleep quality and recovery. Split AM plus PM for doses above 3 IU per day.
Store the reconstituted vial upright in the refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 14 to 28 days, depending on the product label. Do not freeze.
Alternative Routes
Subcutaneous (SC)
Reference route: no adjustment needed
Bioavailability ~70–80%. Slower absorption than IM but steady, sustained serum levels. Abdomen preferred; thigh and glute acceptable. Rotate injection sites systematically.
Intramuscular (IM)
No US label gives an IM dose; one study found higher exposure IM than SC (PMID 1490668)

Faster Tmax than SC (3 h vs 4 to 6 h) and higher total exposure (AUC 194 vs 134 ng·h/mL) in 12 healthy volunteers (PMID 1490668). More painful. Not standard in clinical or community settings. Occasionally used by bodybuilders for convenience.
Intravenous (IV)
100% bioavailability vs ~70–80% SC; dose may need downward adjustment
Used in PK studies and hospital GHD diagnostic testing. Not appropriate for home or community use. Risk of rapid GH surge and acute side effects.
Works With
IGF-1 LR3

HGH raises hepatic IGF-1 production systemically; adding IGF-1 LR3 amplifies local downstream anabolic signaling directly in muscle tissue. Commonly cycled 4 weeks on / 4 weeks off within a longer HGH cycle to enhance muscle building without continuous supraphysiological IGF-1.
IGF-1 LR3 20–50 mcg post-workout SC, 4 weeks on / 4 weeks off
CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin

Occasionally added to exogenous HGH to preserve pulsatile GH signaling or as a lower-cost alternative layer. Largely redundant with exogenous HGH in place: some users prefer it as a replacement rather than a stack. If stacked, monitor IGF-1 closely as combined effect can be supraphysiological.
CJC-1295 No DAC + Ipamorelin blend pre-bed SC at reduced doses (100 mcg each); optional add-on only
Tesamorelin

Primarily used as an alternative to HGH for visceral fat reduction (FDA-approved for HIV-associated lipodystrophy). Rarely co-administered with HGH: used in place of it. If combined in advanced protocols, monitor IGF-1 closely.
Avoid
Exogenous insulin

Advanced bodybuilders combine insulin with HGH for extreme anabolism, but insulin + GH dramatically increases risk of life-threatening hypoglycemia. GH blunts insulin sensitivity (raising glucose), which can mask early hypoglycemic warning signs when exogenous insulin is co-administered. Not appropriate for beginners under any circumstances.
Somatostatin analogs (octreotide, lanreotide, pasireotide)
Somatostatin directly inhibits GH secretion and opposes HGH's GH-receptor activity downstream. Co-administration negates HGH efficacy. Clinically used intentionally to block GH in acromegaly.
Oral estrogen (OCP or oral HRT)
Oral estrogen reduces hepatic GH sensitivity and IGF-1 response significantly. May require 2× higher dose to achieve equivalent IGF-1 elevation. Transdermal estrogen has substantially less impact.
Chronic glucocorticoids (prednisone, dexamethasone)
Chronic glucocorticoid use reduces GH efficacy and may unmask adrenal insufficiency: GH can impair cortisol synthesis. Patients on long-term steroids using HGH need adrenal function monitoring.

Insulin resistance is the most clinically important risk with HGH 191AA. At doses of 2 IU per day or higher, fasting blood glucose can rise 10 to 20 mg/dL. The Norditropin FDA label lists new-onset type 2 diabetes and impaired glucose tolerance as labeled adverse events. Fasting glucose monitoring is mandatory, especially in the first eight weeks. If fasting glucose consistently reaches 100 mg/dL, dose reduction or discontinuation is warranted. HbA1c should be checked at baseline and every three to six months on-cycle to catch cumulative glucose dysregulation. Carpal tunnel syndrome is fully dose-dependent. Numbness and tingling in the hands appear most often at 2 IU per day or above. The mechanism involves fluid retention in the carpal tunnel sheath compressing the median nerve. Symptoms typically resolve within two to four weeks after dose reduction. A wrist splint at night helps during acute episodes. Pushing through this symptom at higher doses risks nerve damage. Water retention and peripheral edema are common during the first four to eight weeks. Hands, feet, and face are the most affected areas. Sodium restriction and pre-bed timing (instead of morning injection) can reduce severity. This side effect generally stabilizes as the body adapts, but it's the primary quality-of-life complaint in early weeks. Supraphysiological IGF-1 is a real long-term concern. Chronically raised IGF-1 above age-normal ranges is associated with increased cancer risk and acromegalic changes (jaw thickening, extremity enlargement). IGF-1 labs are the single most important monitoring tool. Target the upper half of normal for age; avoid sustained levels above 350 ng/mL. Gray-market quality introduces additional risks that pharmaceutical-grade product doesn't carry. High dimer content (improperly bonded GH molecules) increases side effects while reducing efficacy. Bacterial endotoxins from poor manufacturing can cause injection-site reactions, fever, and systemic inflammation. This is not a hypothetical concern; it's the most common source of disproportionate side effects reported in community forums. Injection site lipohypertrophy (hardened lumps under the skin) develops when the same spot is used repeatedly. Rotating injection sites across abdomen quadrants, thighs, and glutes prevents this. Never inject the same location more than once per week. Thyroid function can shift during use. GH increases peripheral conversion of T4 to T3, which may drop Free T4 levels and unmask subclinical hypothyroidism. Anyone on levothyroxine should get a thyroid panel at baseline and mid-cycle. Intracranial hypertension is a label warning that's easy to miss. Headache, vision changes, nausea or vomiting can signal it, usually within the first 8 weeks. Labels call for an eye exam before starting and periodically after, and stopping if papilledema shows up. US label contraindications: active malignancy, active proliferative or severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and acute critical illness after major surgery, trauma or respiratory failure. Also listed: children with Prader-Willi syndrome who are severely obese, have a history of upper airway obstruction or sleep apnea, or have severe respiratory impairment. Hypersensitivity to somatropin or its excipients is on the list, as is growth use in children whose epiphyses have closed. A past cancer isn't on that list, but labels require it to be inactive and fully treated first. Pregnancy isn't either; labels say the human data are too limited to judge the risk.
Common Issues & Solutions
Water retention / hand and foot edema: reduce dose by 0.5–1 IU/day; try pre-bed timing instead of AM injection; sodium restriction helps; typically improves after weeks 6–8 as body adapts.

Carpal tunnel (numbness/tingling in hands): fully dose-dependent: reduce by 0.5–1 IU/day; symptoms resolve in 2–4 weeks post-reduction; wrist splint at night relieves acute symptoms; do not push through this at higher doses.

Fasting glucose elevation / insulin resistance: lower dose or split AM + PM to reduce peak; avoid high-glycemic foods in the 2-hour post-injection window; if FBG consistently ≥ 100 mg/dL, reduce dose or discontinue.
IGF-1 above upper-normal range for age: mandatory dose reduction: supraphysiological IGF-1 is associated with cancer risk and acromegalic changes; target upper-normal, not maximum possible.
Injection site lipohypertrophy (lumps, hard spots): rotate injection sites systematically: abdomen quadrants, both thighs, glutes; never inject the same spot more than once per week.

HGH 191AA: Product Quality high risk

"HGH 191AA" sold through gray-market research channels is entirely unregulated. Common issues include: mislabeled or underdosed vials, bacterial endotoxins from poor manufacturing, and high dimer content (two GH molecules improperly bonded: increases side effects, reduces efficacy). Certificate of Analysis claims are often unverifiable. Licensed brands (Genotropin, Humatrope, Norditropin, Omnitrope, Zomacton) are made under FDA oversight. FDA says biologics such as somatropin are not eligible for the 503A and 503B compounding exemptions.

Somatropin (HGH 191AA) is FDA-approved under multiple brand names including Norditropin (Novo Nordisk), Genotropin (Pfizer), Humatrope (Lilly) and Omnitrope (Sandoz). Omnitrope is often called a biosimilar, but FDA's biosimilar list includes no somatropin product. Approved indications include adult growth hormone deficiency, pediatric GHD, Turner syndrome, and several other conditions listed in the respective prescribing information. In the United States, somatropin is a prescription medication. Somatropin is not a federally scheduled controlled substance, but federal law sets a narrower rule for HGH (21 U.S.C. 333(e)). Distributing it, or holding it to distribute, is a crime unless the use treats an FDA-authorized condition on a physician's order. The penalty runs up to 5 years in prison, or 10 if a minor is involved. Since March 23, 2020, FDA has regulated somatropin as a licensed biological product. FDA's March 2020 notice to compounders covers that class. Biological products licensed under section 351 of the PHS Act are not eligible for the 503A and 503B exemptions. A product sold as compounded somatropin is not a licensed product. Gray-market "HGH 191AA" sold as a research chemical has no FDA license. These products are not FDA-regulated, not tested for purity or potency, and carry no manufacturing oversight. Quality varies dramatically by source. Somatropin is banned by WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency) at all times, both in competition and out of competition. Anti-doping tests for GH began in 2004 [5]. The isoform test sees only recent doses, because injected GH clears fast. A biomarker test, accepted by WADA in 2012, was meant to reach further back. That longer window does not appear to have held up in practice [6]. This content is for informational and research purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide or hormone.

phases.notes: Raise by 0.1–0.2 mg (100–200 mcg) every 1–2 months on response and IGF-1. Lower it on adverse reactions or if IGF-1 runs above the age- and sex-normal range. The label's separate weight-based regimen, not for obese patients, caps at 0.016 mg/kg a day (Norditropin label).

protocols.duration: Indefinite with periodic monitoring (GHD is chronic)
protocols.monitoringNotes: IGF-1 every 1–2 months during titration; every 6 months at maintenance. Fasting glucose and HbA1c annually. Thyroid and lipid panel annually.

faqs.q: What is the recommended HGH 191AA dosage?
faqs.a: The calculator uses community-consensus tiers of 200, 500, and 1000 mcg a day. At the WHO international standard of 3 IU per mg, that is about 0.6, 1.5, and 3 IU. Many community protocols run 1 to 4 IU a day. Clinical GHD treatment starts at 0.45 to 0.9 IU a day on the Norditropin label. AACE 2019 guidelines start at 0.3 to 1.5 IU, by age (PMID 31760824). Split doses above 3 IU into morning and afternoon injections to reduce side effects. Community experience consistently supports starting low and titrating up over 4-6 weeks.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of HGH?
faqs.a: Fluid retention leads. In a 6-month Norditropin label trial in adults with GHD, peripheral edema hit 42% vs 8% on placebo. The label calls these effects, carpal tunnel included, usually transient and dose dependent. Joint pain, morning stiffness, and numbness in hands typically appear in weeks 2-4 and often resolve with dose reduction. Insulin resistance is the main long-term concern; fasting glucose monitoring is recommended every 3 months on cycle.

faqs.q: How long does HGH take to work?
faqs.a: Sleep improvement often appears within the first week. Skin quality and recovery benefits show up around weeks 4-6. Body composition changes (fat loss, muscle density) typically become measurable at 8-12 weeks. Full results require 4-6 months of consistent dosing.

faqs.q: Is HGH 191AA the same as pharmaceutical somatropin?
faqs.a: HGH 191AA refers to the 191-amino-acid recombinant human growth hormone, which is the same sequence used in pharmaceutical brands like Norditropin, Genotropin, and Omnitrope. The difference is manufacturing quality. Pharmaceutical brands go through FDA-regulated production; gray-market 191AA varies widely in purity, with third-party testing showing 82-100% purity across brands.

Lyophilized (powder) vials stay stable at 2-8 degrees C for 18-24 months. Once reconstituted, refrigerate and use within 14 to 28 days, depending on the product label. The Genotropin label allows 28 days; the Zomacton 5 mg vial allows 14. Once in use, a Norditropin FlexPro pen keeps 4 weeks in the fridge or 3 weeks at room temperature (up to 25 degrees C). Never freeze reconstituted HGH.
HGH 191AA typically comes in 3.3mg or 5mg vials. Add 1mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of HGH 191AA?
faqs.a: The half-life of HGH 191AA is ~2-4 hours. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: One IU of somatropin costs anywhere from $4 on the gray market to $60 at a brand-name pharmacy. HGH 191AA is the full 191-amino-acid recombinant human growth hormone, identical to what the pituitary gland produces. Multiple FDA-approved brand versions exist (Norditropin, Genotropin, Omnitrope), though most community users source compounded or research-grade product. The Norditropin label starts adults with GHD at 0.45 to 0.9 IU a day. AACE 2019 guidelines start at 0.3 to 1.5 IU, depending on age and health. Community anti-aging and body recomposition protocols push 2 to 4 IU daily, well above clinical dosing. Sleep and recovery improvements show up in the first two weeks; visible fat loss takes six to ten weeks of consistent use.
